carbonated-drinks.desc: Process of making carbonated drinks, in five stages. Stage 1 (water cleaning): raw water passes through a filter and a water softener, where chemicals are added. Stage 2 (heating, evaporation and carbonation): the water is pumped to electric heaters, then passes through a cooling pipe into a carbonation tank, where carbon dioxide is added. Stage 3 (mixing): the carbonated water goes into a mixing tank, where colouring, syrup and flavour are added. Stage 4 (filtering and filling): the drink is filtered and filled into bottles or cans. Stage 5 (packaging): bottles and cans are packed into boxes, loaded onto a delivery truck and taken to supermarkets.

solar-panel.desc: Diagrams showing the structure of a simple solar panel and how it is used. Structure: a box covered by a sheet of transparent glass, with an inlet pipe on one side and an outlet pipe on the other. Use 1: air enters through the inlet, is heated by the sun's rays inside the panel and comes out of the outlet as warm air. Use 2: water enters through the inlet, flows through a zigzag pipe inside the panel where it is heated by the sun, and comes out as warm water.

museum-plan.desc: Floor plans of a museum in 1998 and 2008. 1998: permanent exhibition rooms filled the top left and the right side of the building; a cafe was at the top centre and a garden in the centre; along the bottom were a temporary exhibition room, the tickets/entrance-exit, a shop, WCs and a bags and coats room. 2008: a restaurant has replaced the permanent exhibition area at the top left; the cafe is still at the top, now with WCs next to it; the temporary exhibition room has moved to the middle left; the garden now has a cafe sitting area and fountains; the bags and coats room and the shop have moved to the bottom left beside the tickets/entrance-exit; the permanent exhibition rooms are now only on the right side.

chorleywood.desc: Map of Chorleywood, a village near London, showing development between 1868 and 1994. Main roads run from the north-west to the east and from the north down to the south-west. A railway built in 1909 crosses the village from west to east, with Chorleywood Station in the west-centre. A motorway built in 1970 runs north–south on the east side and meets a main road at a roundabout. Chorleywood Park and Golf Course is in the centre. 1868–1883: a small area just north of the station beside the main road. 1883–1922: an area along the main road around the station. 1922–1970: large areas along the railway to the west and to the south-east of the station. 1970–1994: several areas in the east, around the motorway and the roundabout.

coal-mine.desc: Two maps of a coal mining site. Before redevelopment (a working mine): an office and a staff changing room on the left, a car park in the bottom-left corner, an entrance to the underground mine for workers at the top middle, a medical room in the middle, a lorry park at the bottom middle, and two waste tips on the right. After redevelopment (a visitors' attraction): the office and changing room have become a museum, the car park is unchanged, the mine entrance is now used by visitors, the medical room has become a cafe, the lorry park has been replaced by a souvenir shop, the first waste tip has become a digger driving track, the second has become a picnic area with trees, a children's play area has been added in the bottom-right corner, and a footpath links the new areas.

beachfront.desc: Two maps of a beachfront area in Australia in 1950 and now. 1950: a road from the city ran along the top to a car park on the right; a playground, dining tables and a pavilion were beside the road; there were two 25m pools on the shore, one on each side of the beach, and a lighthouse on the right. Now: the playground has been replaced by a second car park; the road has been extended down the right side to the lighthouse; the dining tables and pavilion remain; a restaurant and a surf club have been built on the left; the left pool has been replaced by a 50m pool; the right 25m pool remains, with a new surf club beside it near the lighthouse.

road-tunnels.desc: Diagrams of two road tunnels in two Australian cities. Tunnel 1 runs under a river (a bridge crosses the river above it) through sand; it is 2.2 km long and labelled 1.5 metres; it was built between 1986 and 1998 at a cost of $555 million and has two tubes, each with two lanes. Tunnel 2 runs under a city centre through stone and clay; it is 3.6 km long and labelled 2.5 metres; it was built between 2002 and 2006 at a cost of $1.1 billion and has two tubes, each with three lanes.
